title: Hodges's lack of showmanship against his applause
summary: Hodges sat sullen and turned his back on audiences, yet won the biggest applause in Ellington's band.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: But see, with Johnny Hodges, you'd go to see Johnny, Johnny would come out there and... He's gonna walk out there...no... He's gonna sit up there like he's mad with the world, and then when his number comes, he's gonna walk out there and stand up at the microphone, he's gonna look at the back of the theatre, and he took the horn up and go on playing, he'll be looking up at the ceiling. But he's gonna

play, and playin' very good. And when he gets through he might bow and he might not bow. I've seen him bring that horn down and turn his back on the audience, and walk back there and sit down. I said, "What kind of showmanship is this?" Turn his back, walk back to his seat and sit down, and don't smile or anything.

Boy, if he had had personality, he would have went over ten times as great as he did. Which I mean, when he got through playing, though, the house would be coming down, boy. He always got the biggest applause of anybody in the band -- including Duke. Duke was no soloist, though. He was really a composer, a leader, but he was no soloist.
